data_requirements: Hourly BTC/USDT closing prices and OHLCV data covering 1 December 2017 to 1 January 2026

training_protocol.early_stopping: validation segment used for early stopping
training_protocol.hyperparameter_tuning: validation segment used for hyperparameter tuning

evaluation_protocol.protocol: rolling walk-forward out-of-sample evaluation with 27 sequential 3-month test folds
evaluation_protocol.position_rule: hold Bitcoin when forecast is positive and remain in cash otherwise, with cost-aware filter suppressing trades unless forecast magnitude exceeds the transaction-cost threshold
evaluation_protocol.transaction_cost: c = 0.001 proportional transaction cost per unit of turnover
evaluation_protocol.main_threshold_interpretation: long-only entry or exit requires forecast magnitude above 0.20%
evaluation_protocol.test_usage: test segment reserved exclusively for final out-of-sample evaluation

preprocessing_protocol.target_construction: forecasting target is one-step-ahead log return from BTC/USDT closing prices
preprocessing_protocol.temporal_causality: features use information available up to and including time t only
preprocessing_protocol.burn_in: December 2017 used as burn-in period for rolling feature construction
preprocessing_protocol.gap_handling: observations near gap timestamps may contain mechanically smoothed returns

strict_requirements: Use the one-step-ahead log return as the prediction target.
Preserve temporal causality: no feature used to predict the next-hour return may depend on information after forecast time t.
Use a rolling walk-forward design with 12-month training, 3-month validation, and 3-month test windows advanced by 3 months.
Use XGBoost with the OHLCV+TA+EGARCH feature set, MSE loss, and loss-best selection for the selected Table 11 row.
Use long-only cost-aware execution with c = 0.001 and lambda = 2.0.
Compute net strategy returns after proportional transaction costs.

This paper investigates whether machine-learning forecasts of hourly BTC/USDT returns can be converted into economically meaningful trading performance after transaction costs.

Each fold contains a 12-month training window, a 3-month validation window, and a 3-month test window. After each fold, the entire window advances by three months. This produces 27 sequential test folds over the out-of-sample evaluation period.
